transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I guess what finally pushed me to make the appointment is that I keep starting follow-up tasks after audits or mentorship events, really meaning to finish them, and then a few days later I realize the final email or review note or form just… never actually got done. It’s starting to cause problems, and I’m frustrated with myself.
Has this difficulty finishing follow-up tasks been a pattern for you since childhood or adolescence, or is this something that started more recently?

It’s definitely not new. I remember it going back to elementary school. My report cards would say things like I was bright, but I lost assignments, rushed through details, talked out of turn, and needed reminders to finish my work.

My mom still jokes that I could do really well on a test but forget the project that was sitting right in my backpack. So… yeah, it’s been a long pattern, not just something that started recently.

Aside from these task-completion issues, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things—like work, health, or relationships—more days than not, and having trouble controlling that worry?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I do get stressed about work and keeping up with things, but I don’t know that I’d call it constant worrying about everything. It feels more like I get frustrated when I realize I’ve dropped the ball.
Over the past two weeks or more, have you noticed a persistent low or sad mood, or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean, I get discouraged when I mess something up or fall behind, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a persistent sad mood for two weeks or lost interest in things I normally enjoy.
Do you notice these same problems with forgetfulness, disorganization, or leaving tasks unfinished in other areas of your life too, like at home or in personal errands, not just at work?

Yes, it happens at home too. It’s not just work.

At work, it’s gotten to the point where mistakes and unfinished follow-up affected a client review, and I’m worried people are starting to question whether I can handle the promotion.

And at home, my husband has had to take over bills or things I agreed to do, because I don’t always follow through reliably. It’s embarrassing, but he can’t really count on me to finish those things without reminders or without them falling through.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out GAD (no excessive/uncontrollable worry) and depressive disorder (no persistent low mood or anhedonia). Symptoms of inattention, disorganization, and forgetfulness confirmed as chronic (since childhood) and pervasive across work and home settings, supporting ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation.
